purpose: Conservative song-specific chip SFX pitch selection from supplied audio
gridAuthority: CACHE_ROAD_SONG_GRID_AUDIT.md; verified 128 BPM / 4/4 / zero origin; unchanged

method.bass: Hann-windowed continuous-frequency DFT (Goertzel), 27.5–82.5 Hz independent peak search; each first beat sampled +60 through +390 ms; separately fit its third harmonic
method.flow: Semitone spectral survey C2–C6 within ±20 cents, 1.25-second Hann windows; strongest bins are spectral evidence and can contain instrument harmonics
notDone: device loudness or subjective musical acceptance

summary.interpretation: Strong D center with recurring F-root first beats in the choruses; Flow independently supports D/A and F coloration. A single major/minor label is less certain than the measured first-beat root map.

confidence.firstBeatRootMap: high: all 100 measured, near equal temperament and independently supported by matching third partial

cueRecommendations.mapping: Use the announced target measure, including preview/count-in across the preceding measure; chorus-local bars 2 and 6 use F, other measures use D.
cueRecommendations.lowerRegister: The same MIDI roots/fifths shifted down 12 semitones suit quiet preparation ticks, locks, engine-idle coloration and softer catches.
cueRecommendations.mostConservative: Root plus octave. Open fifth is an intentionally sparse sound-design voicing, not a transcription of the full backing chord.
cueRecommendations.countIn: Root-root-fifth preparation, resolve root on ONE; short envelopes keep the announced future root from masking any passing bass movement.
cueRecommendations.offBeatSfx: Crashes, skid grit and engine transients should be predominantly noise/FM/pitched sweeps, brief and controlled, rather than arbitrary sustained major chords.
cueRecommendations.avoid: Do not infer F# as a chord third from the D bass's fifth harmonic (~183.54 Hz); do not sustain a blanket major triad or retune the original stems.
